Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ggsaveR (development version)

New features

  • Formats of the same device no longer overwrite each other: when two formats would write to the same file, the size is added to the file names, as in plot_120x80mm_300dpi.png. The new option ggsaveR.size_suffix adds the size to every file (TRUE), only on clashes ("auto", the default) or never (FALSE), and a format can carry its own suffix.
  • New option ggsaveR.variants saves greyscale and simulated colour vision deficiency (deutan, protan, tritan) versions of each plot as PNG files. The new function preview_variants() shows them side by side for interactive checks. The simulations use the colorspace package.
  • New option ggsaveR.dir saves all plots with a relative file name into one folder, created if needed.
  • New option ggsaveR.log appends a row per saved file, with size, resolution, MD5 checksum and plot expression, to a CSV file.
  • New option ggsaveR.embed_max_size (default 5 MB) leaves out the plot object and data when they would make a PNG file too large.
  • New function ggsaveR_options() sets and checks the options and returns the previous values.
  • ggsave() gains the path argument of ggplot2::ggsave(). Previously it was passed through, so the overwrite checks looked at the wrong location.

Breaking changes

  • Embedded data are now stored in separate PNG text chunks: the call and session information as plain text, the data as CSV, and only the plot object as a serialized R object. As a result:
    • read_ggsaveR_data() restores the plot object only with trusted = TRUE, because unserializing can run arbitrary code. The call, data and session information are always safe to read, also from other languages.
    • session_info is the printed sessionInfo() as a string, and plot_data is read back from CSV. Use plot_object$data for the exact data.
    • Files written by ggsaveR 0.1.0 can still be read with trusted = TRUE.

Bug fixes

  • PNG files with metadata (ggsaveR.creator or ggsaveR.embed_data) are now rendered by ggplot2::ggsave() itself and are pixel-identical to files saved without metadata. Previously scale, limitsize, string values of dpi (such as "retina") and the plot’s own background were ignored or failed, the default size was 7 x 7 in rather than the size of the current device, and the resolution was not recorded in the file.
  • An argument given both in the ggsave() call and in ggsaveR.formats (e.g. width) no longer fails with “matched by multiple actual arguments”. The value in the format is used.
  • device can again be a function, as in ggplot2::ggsave().
  • For a single file, filename is used as given. ggsave("Plot.PNG") is no longer renamed to Plot.png, and ggsave("my.plot", device = "png") no longer writes my.png.
  • ggsaveR.overwrite_action = "unique" no longer adds a trailing dot to file names without an extension.
  • When ggsave() is called through do.call(), the recorded call is <plot object> rather than the deparsed plot object.

Other improvements

  • ggsaveR now attaches ggplot2 (it is in Depends), so its ggsave() masks the original whatever the order of the library() calls. Previously, calling library(ggplot2) after library(ggsaveR) silently disabled all enhancements.
  • ggsaveR.formats can be a character vector of devices, e.g. c("png", "pdf").
  • With several formats, "unique" gives all files of one call the same suffix, and "stop" fails before any file is written.
  • Invalid option values now give an error instead of being silently ignored.
  • The message about embedded data reports its size.
  • The creation time is stored under the standard PNG keyword Creation Time (was CreationTime).
  • ragg and svglite are now suggested rather than imported, and rlang is no longer needed. Install svglite to save SVG files.
  • Vignettes are now built with the package; added examples, a package help page (?ggsaveR) and this NEWS file.

ggsaveR 0.1.0

  • Initial version.
